standard_prerequisites.name: Noetherian Chow lemma
standard_prerequisites.relation: the Noetherian engine applied at a finite level

core_obligations: Reduction: closed immersion X -> Y with Y separated fp over S (proposition-separated-closed-in-finite-presentation); Y and S approximated by Noetherian schemes; Y_i of fp with Y = S x_{S_i} Y_i (lemma-descend-finite-presentation) and Y_i -> S_i separated (lemma-descend-separated-finite-presentation).

Generic point control: for i large, h(eta_j) are pairwise distinct and none specializes to another (lemma-topology-limit); the scheme-theoretic image Y' of h has generic points exactly the h(eta_j) (quasi-compact dominance lemmas).
Assembly: apply the Noetherian Chow lemma to Y' -> S_i, pull the diagram back along S -> S_i; X' = X x_{Y'} Y* maps isomorphically to X over the dense open U = h^{-1}(V) containing all eta_j.
proof_roadmap: Closed immersion into fp target; approximate target and base.
Separate the finitely many generic points at a finite level.
Scheme-theoretic image has exactly those generic points.
Noetherian Chow diagram; pull back; density from the generic points.
difficulty_reason: Noetherian approximation assembled from five chapter lemmas plus the Noetherian Chow lemma: closed immersion into an fp Y, approximation of S and Y, generic-point separation via lemma-topology-limit, scheme-theoretic image dominance, then base change of the Noetherian Chow diagram and density of the pullback open.

compared.difference: The finite-type variant without the finitely-many-components hypothesis delivers only the diagram without the dense-open isomorphism; this lemma adds the generic-point argument for the isomorphism over a dense open. Both delivered.
